score_rate.primary_risk: The exact fifth live claim conflates evaluations: arXiv v1 reports LR versus MILP on RSR-Bench, while nonlinear NLA-DigBench compares Bitween against DIG and SymInfer; its cited Table 2 is only a learned post-condition example.

target_claims: Success conditioning is proved to exactly solve a trust-region policy optimization problem with a chi-squared divergence constraint whose radius is determined by the data (Section 4.3).
At the optimum, relative policy improvement, chi-squared policy-change magnitude, and action-influence are shown to be exactly equal at every state (Section 4.4).
The analysis characterizes exact success conditioning as a conservative improvement operator that cannot degrade performance or induce dangerous distribution shift (Section 4.3).
The paper analyzes return thresholding as an extension that can amplify improvement but can misalign the learned policy with the true objective (Section 5).

target_claims: RACO directly applies conflict-averse gradient descent to objective-specific pairwise preference losses instead of relying on explicit reward models (Section 3).
The clipped CAGrad update is introduced to stabilize multi-objective LLM alignment while respecting user-specified objective weights (Section 3.2).
The paper proves convergence of clipped CAGrad to Pareto-critical points that respect user-specified weights in nonconvex smooth settings (Theorem 3.1).
For two objectives, the analysis shows clipping can strictly improve the convergence rate (Theorem 3.2).

target_claims: Exhaustively verify on finite two-response instances that DPO-RLHF equivalence holds under the stated positive-preference condition.
Verify algebraically and over a deterministic parameter grid that DPO rewards improvement relative to the reference policy rather than absolute preferred-response probability.
Construct and enumerate witnesses with delta_ref < delta_policy < 0 where DPO loss improves while the policy still prefers the dispreferred response.
Validate the constrained-RLHF stationarity equations and resulting adaptive reference-based CPO margin on finite response spaces.
Verify the DPO soft-margin-ranking identity and exhibit reference policies producing negative target margins.

claim_bindings.target_claim: Exhaustively verify on finite two-response instances that DPO-RLHF equivalence holds under the stated positive-preference condition.
claim_bindings.challenge_claim: The paper proves DPO-RLHF equivalence is conditional on the RLHF-optimal policy preferring human-preferred responses (Section 3).

claim_bindings.challenge_claim: When the equivalence assumption fails, DPO optimizes relative advantage over the reference policy rather than absolute human-preference alignment (Section 3).

claim_bindings.target_claim: Validate the constrained-RLHF stationarity equations and resulting adaptive reference-based CPO margin on finite response spaces.
claim_bindings.challenge_claim: Constrained Preference Optimization augments RLHF with constraints and derives a stationary DPO-like loss with an adaptive reference-based margin (Section 4.3).

claim_bindings.target_claim: Verify the DPO soft-margin-ranking identity and exhibit reference policies producing negative target margins.
claim_bindings.challenge_claim: The paper gives a soft-margin ranking interpretation showing DPO can implement margin ranking with potentially negative targets (Section 5).

target_claims: Mechanistic Data Attribution quantifies individual training-sample influence on targeted interpretable LLM units such as induction and previous-token heads (Figure 1, Table 3).
Targeted deletion or augmentation of high-influence samples causally modulates induction-head and previous-token-head emergence more than random interventions (Figure 2).
High-influence samples for induction heads are concentrated in repetitive structural domains, with top-ranked examples including LaTeX, HTML, and repeated text patterns (Table 1, Figure 4).
